title: Extraction plan
description: What the engine found in every document routed to a schedule. Reading a document and working out its transactions is one generic skill, whatever the format, so the primary output is the rows themselves, in read_directly. A mapping in tables is only a shortcut the engine may choose for a very long table: it names which column means which field, and code reads every row. Every document routed to the schedule must appear in exactly one of the three lists.

read_directly.description: Documents the engine read itself, with every transaction it found for this schedule. Any format: PDF statement, Word export, text, short spreadsheet.

file.description: File name exactly as given in the listing.

rows.description: One entry per transaction, in this schedule's row shape. Empty when the document was read and holds nothing for this schedule.

why.description: What the document is, and where in it the rows came from.

tables.description: Column mappings for tables too long to transcribe. Code reads every row against the mapping.

file.description: File name exactly as given in the listing.

header_row.description: 1-based row number holding the column headers.

asset_class.description: Applied to every row of this table when the table is single-class, e.g. an equity sheet.

asset_class_column.description: Use instead of asset_class when the table itself names the class per row.

columns.description: schema field -> column header. Omit a field the table does not carry. A money field may instead name a LIST of headers, and code adds those columns together for each row: use it where a table spreads one figure over several columns, such as selling charges over brokerage, exchange charges and GST. Leave STT out of any such list.

require_columns.description: Rows where any of these is blank are skipped. Use it to drop sub-headers, totals and blank separators.

stop_at_blank.description: Stop at the first fully blank row after the header, for sheets holding several stacked tables.

excluded.description: Documents or sheets that contribute no rows, each with the kind of reason, so code never has to infer intent from prose.

kind.description: duplicate: another listed document holds the same material (name it in why). other_schedule: belongs elsewhere (name the schedule). summary_only: aggregates used only for reconciliation. no_transactions: read, and holds nothing for this schedule. unreadable: could not be opened or read -- a gap in the return, not a choice.
